name: Dark Greyish Lavender
lede: Dark Greyish Lavender is a dark greyish shade of [[lavender|lavender]], one of Robert Ridgway's working names built by the plain grammar of modifier plus base color.

sections.title: A modifier, not a new color
sections.body: Dark Greyish Lavender stacks two modifiers, *dark* and *greyish*, onto the base color [[lavender]], named for the flower [1][4]. Ridgway's 1912 plate XLIII, hue 57-triple-prime, is also reached by a near neighbor on the same plate, hue 53-triple-prime, in our sources [1]. The ISCC-NBS system calls the matching block, 214, 'pale violet,' the closest match of any name, a Delta-E of just 1.8 [2]. The nearest named colors on file are [[light-dull-bluish-violet]], [[manatee]] and [[light-hyssop-violet]], at 3.5, 5.1 and 5.3 ΔE [1][4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this shade, as photographed, in 0.35% of 23,781 paintings, 84 paintings; within a single canvas it reads as a distinct area in 37 of them [3]. That makes it rarer than 54% of the archive's named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, found in 0.5% of that century's 1,674 paintings, 2.0 times the expected rate [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color, by lightness rank, in 41% of its 37 appearances [3]. The earliest dated appearance is a 1520 painting by Antonio da Correggio, 392 years before the name's first documented record in 1912; the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor and not a first [3]. It is most over-represented in paintings from France, 2.3 times the expected rate, 13 of 3,443 French paintings in our archive [3].
